definition: Split Up is an intelligent decision support system, which makes predictions about the distribution of marital property following divorce in Australia.
details: It is designed to assist judges, registrars of the Family Court of Australia, mediators and lawyers. Split Up operates as a hybrid system, combining rule – based reasoning with neural network theory. Rule based reasoning operates within strict parameters, in the form: IF < condition(s) > then <action>. Neural networks, by contrast, are considered to be better suited to generate decisions in uncertain domains, since they can be taught to weigh the factors considered by judicial decision makers from case data. Yet, they do not provide an explanation for the conclusions they reach. Split_up, with a view to overcome this flaw, uses argument structures proposed by Toulmin as the basis for representations from which explanations can be generated.

explainer.lead: Split Up is an intelligent decision support system that predicts the distribution of marital property after divorce in Australia. It matters because it supports judges, registrars of the Family Court of Australia, mediators and lawyers in a consequential domain.

tiers.eli5: It's a computer advisor that helps work out how property might be split in a divorce, giving people in the legal process a starting point.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers built it as a hybrid combining rule-based reasoning with neural network theory: rules apply strict IF-condition-then-action parameters, while networks handle uncertain domains by weighing factors as judicial decision makers do. A pitfall is that the two mechanisms have different strengths, so the split of duties matters.
tiers.paperLevel: A hybrid decision support system: rule-based reasoning operates within strict parameters of the form IF conditions then action, while neural networks generate decisions in uncertain domains by learning to weigh the factors considered by judicial decision makers.

explainer.example: For a case, the rule-based component applies fixed parameters while the neural component weighs the factors to produce a prediction about property distribution.
